text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Retired police chief Philip Kilonzo drops dead at his hotel in Machakos district, eastern Kenya, while having drink with friend.
- Uganda formally protests against detention and harassment of its nationals in Kenya.
- Kenneth Matiba, chairman of opposition FORD-Asili party, calls for fresh census and revision of constituency boundaries before general election scheduled for later this year.
- Matiba reiterates earlier stand that National Convention Executive Council has no mandate to represent opposition in talks with government on constitutional reforms.
- Government to establish factory to make military hardware, machinery and equipment in Eldoret, Rift Valley.
- Vice-President Saitoti says government is more committed to constitutional reforms than opposition.
- Protracted tussle over parentage of teenage Somali girl Abdia Derow Garad ends after she declares that one of the claimants to her parentage was her biological mother.
- National Social Security Fund will no longer invest in real estate -- move aimed at streamlining national pension fund's investment activities which previously have been criticised heavily.
